tasks.title: The P gain with TPA
tasks.solution: calculateMultirotorTPAFactor: factor = (100 − tpa_rate · (throttle − breakpoint) / (2000 − breakpoint)) / 100 at a throttle above the breakpoint. kP = mc_p / 31 · factor. On a multirotor TPA attenuates P, D and CD but not I. tpa_rate must not be set above 100 on a multirotor: the factor at high throttle becomes negative, and P and D change sign.

tasks.title: Rotation rate from the stick position
tasks.solution: rc_curves.c: rcCommand = lrint(500 · s · (1 − e · (1 − s²))), e = rc_expo / 100; then ω = rcCommand / 500 · roll_rate · 10. The rate is in tens of °/s; expo changes the shape of the curve but not the maximum. An answer without rounding rcCommand to an integer differs by no more than 1 °/s — it is accepted too.

tasks.title: EZ Tune: pitch P from the sliders
tasks.solution: ez_tune.c: roll P = 40 · response / 100, pitch P = 40 · response / 100 · axis_ratio / 100; the result is written to an integer, and the fractional part is dropped. The base for I is 75, for D — 23, for CD — 100.

tasks.title: The horizontal acceleration limit in navigation
tasks.solution: Navigation converts acceleration to an angle: θ = atan(a / g), so a_max = g · tan θ. At 35° that is 6.87 m/s²; at 45° — 9.81 m/s², which is also the hard limit of the code (980 cm/s²).

tasks.title: Braking distance and the stop point
tasks.solution: The target is placed v · nav_mc_pos_deceleration_time / 100 meters ahead. The minimum distance at a constant deceleration a = g · tan θ is v² / (2a). The difference is the margin; the real distance is longer than the calculated one because the acceleration builds up with the jerk limit of 1700 cm/s³.

variants.statement: The aircraft flies at 12 m/s, nav_mc_bank_angle = 30, nav_mc_pos_deceleration_time = 150. Assuming that it brakes at once with the maximum acceleration g · tan θ, find by how many meters the stop target (velocity × time) is farther than the minimum braking distance. A negative answer means that the aircraft overshoots the target. (g = 9.80665)
